Que proposent les partis à propos du rac: What are the parties proposing on systemic racism?
Certaines questions, surtout d’ordre soc: Some issues, especially social ones, are barely addressed by the party leaders in this election.
Afin de mettre en lumière un enjeu un pe: To shed light on an issue that has been discussed a little less in this election campaign, I set out to research the fight against systemic racism. It was a very present issue in the 2021 election campaign, and I wanted to know how the parties are approaching it this year.
Un constat s'impose : une absence de mes: One finding stands out: a lack of specific measures in the parties’ election platforms.
La question de la guerre commerciale ave: The trade war with the United States is on everyone’s lips in this election campaign. Canadians are looking for a leader capable of standing up to the threat posed by Donald Trump. However, some issues, especially social ones, are barely addressed by the party leaders.
Lors des élections de 2021,<l1> la quest: In the 2021 election,<l1> the question of systemic racism was almost central.</l1> As a reminder, the death of George Floyd, the death of Joyce Echaquan and the discovery of unmarked graves at Indigenous residential schools brought to light the government’s responsibility for inequality and racism. Four years later, the issue is rarely found in the parties’ election platforms. After examining them closely, we found a few scattered measures, but also, at times, challenges to existing provisions on systemic racism.
<strong>Parti Libéral : un plan global m: Liberal Party: a comprehensive plan, but few concrete elements
Contrairement à Justin Trudeau, le Parti: Unlike Justin Trudeau, the Liberal Party, under Mark Carney’s leadership, proposes fairly general measures that target few or no communities in particular. Overall, the plan set out in the election platform does express a desire to fight racism and sexism and to support LGBTQ+ communities, but without developing specific measures.
<strong>Les promesses des libéraux pour: The Liberals’ promises to fight systemic racism:
Le parti libéral souhaite lutter contre: The Liberal Party wants to fight the rise of hate by implementing the <l1>Canada’s Action Plan on Combatting Hate</l1> put in place under Trudeau in 2024. The party proposes to continue implementing this measure,
Le Parti propose aussi d’augmenter de fa: The party also proposes to significantly increase the annual budget of the Canada Community Security Program to help protect vulnerable communities and places of worship. The amount allocated to this program is not specified, however,
Il dit vouloir défendre la Charte canadi: It says it wants to defend the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms. It also proposes to protect the values on which the Charter is founded and to guarantee the protection of women, people with disabilities, racialized communities, Indigenous people and 2SLGBTQI+ people.
<strong>Nouveau parti démocratique : un: New Democratic Party: a focus on Indigenous issues
Sur sa plateforme électorale, le parti d: In its election platform, Jagmeet Singh’s party offers few measures on the fight against inequality and injustice in the broader sense. The party chooses to put reconciliation with First Nations at the centre of the debate, building a plan around this issue. It proposes to launch a national inquiry into systemic violence and racism against Indigenous peoples within Canadian institutions.
<strong>Bloc Québécois : identité provin: Bloc Québécois: provincial identity and rejection of certain federal equity policies
En termes de stratégie électorale, le pa: In terms of electoral strategy, Yves-François Blanchet’s party focuses on promoting Quebec identity. In the section of its platform titled “Choisir d’être nous-mêmes” (“Choosing to be ourselves”), the following measures can be found:
Le Bloc Québécois vise une plus grande p: The Bloc Québécois aims for greater participation of minorities in public institutions, but proposes to abolish equity, diversity and inclusion criteria in the federal apparatus, because they create exclusion and are ill-suited to the realities of Quebec and its regions,
Le parti travaillera à la mise en place: The party will work to set up an ombudsman against discrimination in all its forms in federally regulated institutions,
Le Bloc souhaite déposer un projet de lo: The Bloc wants to table a bill to exclude Quebec from Canadian multiculturalism so that the province can choose its own model for integrating newcomers.
Le Bloc propose de retirer le financemen: The Bloc proposes to withdraw funding for equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) initiatives in the federal public service.
Les politiques EDI sont des initiatives: EDI policies are federal initiatives aimed at reducing the systemic barriers and biases faced by Canadian minority groups. The goal is to put in place a fairer, more just and more diverse system in research and in access to employment and services. The party’s financial framework does not specify what such a cut would amount to. In the section New revenues and savings, the party plans to devote $21,475 million over five years to the Public service and consultants.
Dans sa quête du renforcement des valeur: In its quest to strengthen Quebec values across Canada, the Bloc Québécois favours a whole series of measures in support of the Act respecting the laicity of the State in Quebec, Bill 21. Those most affected by the implementation and strengthening of this law, notably members of Quebec’s Muslim and Jewish communities, believe these measures go against the principles of equality and the fight against systemic racism.
Le Bloc Québécois souhaite supprimer le: The Bloc Québécois wants to eliminate the position of Canada’s Special Representative on Combatting Islamophobia. It would amend the definition of the duties of Canada’s Special Envoy on Preserving Holocaust Remembrance and Combatting Antisemitism, in order to keep the mandates arising from international commitments, while removing its role as adviser to the prime minister and ministers,
Le parti souhaite interdire le port de s: The party wants to ban the wearing of religious symbols by federal employees in positions of authority who work in Quebec, in line with the framework established by Bill 21,
Le Bloc Québécois s’opposera fermement à: The Bloc Québécois will firmly oppose any federal challenge to Quebec’s Bill 21,
Le parti souhaite agir pour encadrer la: The party wants to act to regulate prayer in federal public spaces, notably airports.
<strong>Parti Vert du Canada : un engage: Green Party of Canada: a clear commitment
Le parti, codirigé par Jonathan Pedneaul: The party, co-led by Jonathan Pedneault and Elizabeth May, takes a concrete position with a series of measures to fight climate change and the social inequalities linked to systemic racism. However, these promises are not costed.
Lancer une enquête nationale sur le raci: Launch a national inquiry into systemic racism in police services, including into recent deaths of people in custody and the disproportionate use of force against First Nations,
Mettre en place un bureau permanent de l: Set up a permanent, high-level office of environmental justice within Environment Canada. It would be responsible for implementing Canada’s national strategy on racism and environmental justice,
Renforcer les lois contre les discours e: Strengthen laws against hate speech and hate groups,
Financer des programmes communautaires d: Fund community programs to fight discrimination,
Lutter contre les pratiques racistes dan: Fight racist practices in police and law enforcement services: require judges to explicitly consider systemic racism when determining sentences, in line with Supreme Court rulings.
<strong>Parti Conservateur Canadien : Un: Conservative Party of Canada: a platform without measures for inclusion
Le parti de Pierre Poilièvre n’a pas de: Pierre Poilievre’s party has no specific plan to fight hate, discrimination or the exclusion of various minority groups. As a rule, its election platform focuses essentially on economic development issues. The Conservative Party says it wants to end the imposition of woke ideology in the federal public service and in the allocation of federal funds for university research. Asked on Mario Dumont’s show on QUB about the position of Canada’s Special Representative on Combatting Islamophobia, Pierre Poilievre replied that he did not want to reserve a position for one particular group of people. He said he was against “any kind of racism,” but did not endorse the Liberal Party’s “woke approach.” No measure on whether or not to abolish the position appears in the party’s election platform. Like the Bloc Québécois, the Conservatives want to reduce funding for equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) initiatives in the federal public service, according to the Public Service Alliance of Canada. Once again, nothing in the party’s financial framework specifies the amount of this potential cut.
